sections.title: First fugue: subject I
sections.text: A ricercar in long notes. Begin quietly and let each entry add a voice; the subject is the line to hear, the others accompany it.

sections.title: Second fugue: subject II
sections.text: Running quavers and semiquavers: lighter, more speaking. Keep the semiquavers even and legato in small groups; do not let them cover the longer notes.

sections.title: Subjects I and II together
sections.text: The first subject returns against the second: two characters at once. Give subject I its weight and length while II keeps moving.

sections.title: Third fugue: B-A-C-H
sections.text: The composer's name in notes (B flat, A, C, B natural). A new, chromatic colour: more inward, never forced.

sections.title: All three subjects
sections.text: The three subjects sound together for the first time; then the manuscript breaks off. Voice it so that all three are heard; how to end a performance (stop in silence, or close another way) is the players' decision.
